rationale: The pain is a real but niche network engineering annoyance — Chrome HTTP/2 connection pooling conflicts with VPN state changes — and the buyer (platform engineers, DevOps) is only moderately clear. Critically, the solution requires either a browser extension (Chrome store approval, ongoing maintenance, distribution challenges) or a smart proxy middleware (per-environment deployment, custom configuration per company), neither of which is buildable as a Claude prompt plus a landing page, and neither can run autonomously. Willingness to pay is very weak: there are no paid substitutes and the workaround is a browser restart. Total of 3.6 is well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: A solo non-technical operator could not realistically build or maintain this. The solution requires either systems-level network proxy code or a browser extension with deep Chrome networking API access — both require real software engineering. Even if built, selling to DevOps/platform engineers requires technical credibility and a free tier to prove value, and support would require hands-on debugging of customer network environments. Drop this entirely.
notes: Total 3.6 well below min_total_to_validate (5.5). Fails buildability_with_ai (3 < 6), operational_autonomy (3 < 7), buyer_clarity (4 < 6), and willingness_to_pay (3 < 5). All four build gates fail.
